Radhakrishnan Releases Updated Constitution of India in Sindhi Language Vice President of India C. P. Radhakrishnan released the updated edition of the Constitution of India in Sindhi language in both Devanagari Script (1st edition) and Persian Script (2nd edition) in Uparashtrapati Bhawan, New Delhi, Delhi, on the occasion of Sindhi Language Day (Sindhi Bhasha Diwas) on April 10, 2026, promoting linguistic inclusivity by making constitutional provisions accessible in citizens’ mother tongues. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Constitution of India released in Sindhi language ✓ By whom? Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan ✓ When? On the occasion of Sindhi Language Day on April 10, 2026 ✓ Scripts: Devanagari (1st edition), Persian (2nd edition) ✓ Inclusion: Sindhi language included via 21st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1967. ✓ Previous translations: Bodo, Dogri, Santhali, Tamil, Gujarati, Nepali. ✓ Ministry: Ministry of Law and Justice (MoL&J) About the Constitution in Sindhi Language: Significance: The initiative enhances accessibility, inclusivity, and democratic participation for Sindhi speakers. Authority: The initiative is implemented by the Legislative Department under the MoL&J in line with Articles 343, 345, and 350B, while Sindhi’s inclusion in the Eighth Schedule through the 21st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1967 affirms its cultural significance. Translations: Part of a wider initiative translating the Constitution into languages like Bodo, Dogri, Santhali, Tamil, Gujarati, and Nepali. Vision: Strengthens democracy, bridges governance gaps, and supports linguistic diversity aligned with the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. INTERNATIONAL AFFAIRS India–Uzbekistan Joint Military Exercise DUSTLIK 2026 Begins in Namangan On April 12 2026, the Seventh edition of the India–Uzbekistan Joint Exercise, ‘DUSTLIK 2026’, officially commenced at Gurumsaray Field Training Area in Namangan, Uzbekistan. • The 13-day exercise is being conducted from April 12 to 25, 2026. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Exercise DUSTLIK 2026 Begins ✓ Edition: 7th ✓ Between: India–Uzbekistan ✓ Where? Namangan, Uzbekistan ✓ Objective: Enhance interoperability, joint planning & defence cooperation ✓ Participants: o IA (45 personnel), IAF (15 personnel) o Uzbekistan Air Force: 15 personnel ✓ Focus: Counter-terrorism, special operations in semi-mountainous terrain. Background: Origin: Exercise DUSTLIK, meaning ‘Friendship’ in Uzbek, is a Bilateral military exercise initiated in 2019, involving joint training between the Indian and Uzbekistan Joint Army and Air Forces. Nature: It is an annual exercise conducted alternately in India and Uzbekistan to strengthen bilateral defence cooperation. Previous Edition: The 6th edition of the India-Uzbekistan Joint Exercise DUSTLIK 2025 was held at Foreign Training Node, Aundh in Pune (Maharashtra). About Exercise DUSTLIK: Objective: To strengthen military cooperation and enhance joint operational capabilities in semi- mountainous terrain, focusing on physical fitness, joint planning, tactical drills, and special arms skills, while also developing a unified command-and-control framework for effective execution of joint operations. Focus: The exercise will cover land navigation, strike operations on enemy bases, and capture of enemy- held areas, along with mutual exchange of operational practices between the Indian contingent and the Uzbekistan Armed Forces.

BANKING & FINANCE RBI Unveiled Utkarsh 2029 targets digital currency, UPI global expansion drive In April 2026, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) unveiled its medium-term strategy, Utkarsh 2029 for April 2026 to March 2029, aimed to consolidate its position as a world-class, full-service central bank. • The newly launched strategy for 2029 outlines 49 deliverables across 6 pillars: robust regulations, customer centricity and inclusive finance, competitive markets, effective technology, future-ready organisation and global integration. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Unveiling of Utkarsh 2029 ✓ Unveiled by: RBI ✓ Time Period: April 2026 to March 2029

# Page 32^page=32
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 32 Daily Content PDF ✓ Total Deliverables: 49 ✓ Key Pillars: 06 (robust regulations, customer centricity and inclusive finance, competitive markets, effective technology, future-ready organisation and global integration) ✓ Key Objectives: Advancement of Project Sa-Mudra, expand the use of CBDC, scaling-up of the ULI, purpose-built Large Language Model (LLM), among others. Key Objectives of Utkarsh 2029: Project Sa-Mudra: The framework plans to advance Project Sa-Mudra to modernise currency management systems. CBDC Expansion: The strategy also plans to expand the use of Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC), enabling more efficient cross-border payments. ULI Framework: It also emphasizes the scaling-up of the Unified Lending Interface (ULI) to enhance access to credit, particularly for underserved segments. ULI is designed to enable “frictionless credit” by facilitating the flow of digital information from various data providers to lenders. Indigenous-built LLM: It also plans to develop an indigenous Artificial Intelligence (AI) tool based on purpose-built Large Language Model (LLM)for its internal operations. Focus on Emerging Technologies: It plans to issue a framework on the use of AI in the financial sector due to increasing deployment of AI across credit underwriting, fraud detection and customer engagement. Sandboxes: The framework also aims to expand asset tokenisation and set up Digital and AI sandboxes, supporting innovation in a controlled environment. International Use of Rupee: The strategy further aims to support the international use of the Indian Rupee (INR) for trade settlements. Global Expansion of UPI: Apart from INR, the RBI also plans to promote the implementation of the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) stack in other countries. Supervisory Tools (DAKSH): The enhancement of the ‘DAKSH’ (Advanced Supervisory Monitoring System) as part of this roadmap. Green Finance: The Utkarsh 2029 includes a commitment to Climate Risk and Sustainable Finance, specifically creating a framework for “green” financial disclosures. Others: The strategy also includes the deployment of technology-led supervisory tools and promotes responsible innovation and ethical use of technology in the financial sector. • It emphasizes the complete digitalisation of RBI internal processes which means elimination of paper-based workflows or e-mail-based interactions. About Reserve Bank of India (RBI): Governor- Dr. Sanjay Malhotra Headquarters- Mumbai, Maharashtra Established in- April, 1935 SEBI Launches Three New IT platforms to Transform Regulatory Landscape In March 2026, Tuhin Kanta Pandey, chairman of Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) launched three new Information Technology (IT) platforms: SUPCOMS (Single Universal Platform for Communications) 2.1; Electronic(e)-adjudication portal; and Cyber-Sec Audit Compliance (C-SAC), to boost ease of doing business and strengthen cybersecurity oversight. • These digital initiatives aimed to streamline communication, enable digital quasi-judicial proceedings, and enhance cybersecurity supervision of SEBI-regulated entities. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Launch of 3 New IT Platforms ✓ Launched by: Tuhin Kanta Pandey, Chairman of SEBI ✓ Platform Names: SUPCOMS 2.1, e-adjudication portal and C-SAC

# Page 33^page=33
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 33 Daily Content PDF ✓ Purpose: To streamline communication, enable digital quasi-judicial proceedings, and enhance cybersecurity supervision of SEBI-regulated entities. Key Details of IT Platforms: SUPCOMS 2.1: This newly launched single universal digital platform replaces traditional Electronic mail (email)-based communication with SEBI, ensuring all interactions with external entities are centrally accessible and streamlined. • The platform creates a robust institutional memory, maintains an audit trail, and eliminates fragmented exchanges or broken reply chains. • It is live on the SEBI eServices portal and is accessible by registered intermediaries and external entities via login. e-Adjudication Portal: It provides a transparent and paperless platform for quasi-judicial proceedings, enhancing efficiency and speed in adjudication matters. • Some of the key features of this new digital platform: Access and download Show Cause Notices (SCNs); submit replies, post-hearing documents, and requests (e.g., inspection, extension of time) and participate in online hearings through a dedicated module. • The portal is integrated with SEBI’s internal Case Management System (CMS) to streamline workflows across departments and is operational and available online for market participants, with detailed guidelines provided. Cyber-Sec Audit Compliance (C-SAC): It is an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based platform that enables automated analysis of cyber audit reports to identify compliance gaps, risk areas, and actionable insights. • The system enhances efficiency, reduces manual effort, and supports data-driven supervision, strengthening SEBI’s risk-based supervision and cybersecurity oversight. About Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI): Background: Prior to the establishment of SEBI, the Indian securities market was regulated by the Controller of Capital Issues (CCI), a body established under the Capital Issues (Control) Act of 1947. Formation: The SEBI was founded as the regulating authority for the Indian securities market on April 12, 1992, by the SEBI Act 1992. Regional Presence: The organisation has regional offices in New Delhi (Delhi), Ahmedabad (Gujarat), Kolkata (West Bengal, WB), and Chennai (Tamil Nadu, TN). Composition: SEBI is governed by a Board of Directors responsible for regulating the securities market, comprising a Chairman appointed by the Government of India (GoI), two members from the Ministry of Finance (MoF), one member from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), and five members nominated by the government (at least three full-time). ECONOMY & BUSINESS ADB Raises India’s GDP Forecast for FY27 to 6.9% In April 2026, Asian Development Bank (ADB) released its latest “Asian Development Outlook (ADO) April 2026: The Middle East Conflict Challenges Resilience in Asia and the Pacific”. The report raised India’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth forecast for Financial Year 2026-27 (FY27) by 40 basis points (bps) to 6.9% from its previous estimate of 6.5% and also lower than 7.6% estimated for FY26. • This growth projection is driven by higher consumption, higher investment, supportive policies and recent trade agreements. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Asian Development Outlook April 2026 released ✓ Released by: ADB ✓ India GDP: 6.9% (FY27); 7.3% (FY28) ✓ Inflation: 4.5% (FY27); 4% (FY28) ✓ Region Growth: Asia-Pacific at 5.1% (CY26 & CY27). Key Projections: FY28: The report further projected that the Indian economy is expected to grow at 7.3% in FY28, supported by private consumption, revisions to government salaries and pensions, along with continued public investment and favourable external factors. Key Drivers: The report highlighted that on the supply side, sectors like: manufacturing and services are expected to witness robust growth, supported by domestic reforms and favourable access to foreign markets. Financial Indicators: As per the ADB’s latest outlook, central government Capital Expenditure (CAPEX) is projected to increase by 11.5% in FY26, reflecting India’s investment-led growth strategy. • It further highlighted that Current Account Deficit (CAD) is projected to widen in FY27, mainly due to higher imports, especially crude oil prices but is expected to narrow in FY28 as global energy markets stabilize and exports strengthen. Inflation: The report estimated that India’s inflation to more than double from 2.1% (in FY26) to 4.5% (in FY27) due to a rebound in food prices, surge in global crude oil prices, currency weakness, among others. • However, Inflation is projected to ease to 4% in FY28. Region-wise: The report estimated that economic growth in developing Asia and the Pacific region will ease to 5.1% in both Calendar Year 2026 (CY26) and Calendar Year (CY27) compared to 5.4% in CY25.
